transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… it’s mostly this thing with food at night. I’ll start picking at something, and I tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand just keeps going back. It feels like I’m not really the one deciding anymore.
When you're eating at night, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating?
Yeah… that’s the part that bothers me. Once I start, I’ll tell myself, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then I just keep reaching for it anyway. Like I’m not really choosing at that point.
When you're eating at night, do you find yourself eating even when you're not really hungry, or do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
Yeah… I mean, a lot of the time I’m not actually hungry. I already ate dinner with everyone, but later I’ll still go open the fridge and… start up again.
Do you find yourself eating much more quickly than usual during these nighttime eating episodes?
Yeah… I do. It’s not like when I’m eating with my family. I kind of rush through it, like I’m trying to finish before anyone wakes up. I barely even taste it sometimes.
Do these nighttime eating episodes make you feel upset, embarrassed, or do they interfere with your daily life in any way?

A little, yeah. I still get to my shipping and receiving shifts and take care of what I need to. It’s not like I’m missing work. But at home… I’ve started kind of staying away from being in the kitchen with everyone late, because I feel nervous someone’s going to notice how weird I get around the food.
When you're eating at night, do you keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
Yeah… sometimes. By the time I stop, my stomach feels really tight and heavy. I usually just sit there for a while, because lying down or even bending over feels pretty bad.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen after you’ve already gone to bed and fallen asleep?
I’m not really sure… I mean, I don’t think of it that way. Sometimes it’s just later at night, but I don’t know that I’ve already fallen asleep first.
When you eat at night, does it feel like you’re eating all at once in a short period of time, like a defined episode?

Yeah… I guess it can be like that. Some nights after work, I’ll be in the kitchen and it’s like I’m just cleaning up leftovers, but I can end up eating several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and whatever rice or beans are there. It’s usually all in one stretch.
Do you usually eat alone at night because you're embarrassed about how much you're eating or feel like you can't control it?
Yeah… I guess so. I don’t really like anyone seeing how much I’m eating, so I usually wait until my aunt and everyone else is asleep. I try to be quiet in the kitchen.
Is there a point during these nighttime eating times where you realize you’ve eaten a lot more than most people would in one sitting?

Yeah… sometimes I do notice it after. Like, I’ll realize I went through several tamales, a big bowl of pozole, tortillas, and then some rice or beans too. It’s more than someone would normally eat, I guess.
When you're eating at night, does it feel like you're not really in control of yourself, like you're just going through the motions and can't stop even if you want to?

Yeah… that’s kind of what scares me. Once I start picking at stuff late at night, I’ll tell myself, like, “That’s enough, Santiago,” but then my hand just keeps going back. It feels like I’m not really the one deciding anymore.
After you eat a lot at night, do you ever try to get rid of the food by making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual?
No… I don’t do that. I mean, I just feel bad after and try to go to bed. I don’t make myself throw up or anything like that.
Do you ever wake up during the night and eat without really remembering it clearly in the morning?
I don’t think so… I mean, I usually remember getting up and eating. It’s not like I wake up and find out later with no memory or anything.
